learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn how to use pronouns to replace nouns and correctly identify Personal, Demonstrative, Interrogative, and Possessive pronouns.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 Imagine saying: 'Rahul took Rahul's bag and Rahul went to Rahul's school.' Sounds silly and repetitive, right? Enter Pronouns! These are superhero words that swoop in to replace nouns and make our sentences sound smooth.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Personal pronouns take the place of specific people or things. We use First Person (the person speaking), Second Person (the person spoken to), and Third Person (the person/thing spoken about).
examples_or_templates: First Person: I, me, we, us
Third Person: he, she, it, they, them

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Demonstrative pronouns 'point' to specific things (near or far). Possessive pronouns show ownership or who something belongs to (without using an apostrophe!).
examples_or_templates: Possessive: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs

lesson_modules.teaching_content: These are 'W-words' used specifically to ask questions. They stand in for the noun that is the answer to the question.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which pronoun correctly replaces 'The dog' in the sentence: 'The dog is barking loudly'?
❓ Identify the Demonstrative Pronoun in this sentence: 'These are my favorite shoes.'

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with the correct Personal Pronoun: 'Riya is my best friend. ___ is a fantastic singer.'
subjective_practice.hint: Riya is a girl. What third-person pronoun do we use for a singular female?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Change the bold part to a Possessive Pronoun: 'This book **belongs to me**. It is ____.'
✍️ Write an Interrogative Pronoun to complete this question: '____ won the cricket match yesterday?'
subjective_practice.hint: You are asking about a person or a team.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🤐 The 'No Noun' Game
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Pick a famous celebrity or cartoon character. Write 3 sentences describing what they do, but you are NOT allowed to use their actual name! Use pronouns (he, she, it, they) instead. See if your family can guess who it is!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Pronouns are words used in place of nouns to avoid repetition.
⭐ Personal pronouns represent specific people or things (I, you, they).
⭐ Demonstrative point things out (this/that), Possessive show ownership (mine/yours), and Interrogative ask questions (who/what).
